report.summary: The HighRequestErrorRate alert for otel-demo/frontend-proxy is firing because the alert rule's expression is `sum by (service_name, namespace) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{namespace="otel-demo",service_name=~"frontend|frontend-proxy",status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"}[2m])) > 0` held for 180s (the annotation text says "> 3", but the rule uses `> 0`, and the reported value 2.5667 is below 3). The frontend-proxy error spans are HTTP 500/504 on its GET/POST server spans and on its `router frontend egress` client spans toward the frontend, i.e. frontend-proxy is relaying failures produced by the frontend. The frontend's own error spans and logs carry cart-service storage failures: `9 FAILED_PRECONDITION: Can't access cart storage ... Wasn't able to connect to redis`, and checkout reports `cart failure: failed to get user cart during checkout`. The cart pod's own logs show repeated `fail: cart.cartstore.ValkeyCartStore ... Wasn't able to connect to redis` bursts (21:08:39-42, 21:11:19). Those storage errors began only after Deployment valkey-cart (cart's redis backend) was scaled down 1→0 at 21:08:18 (old pod valkey-cart-86cdf6f9b9-z2fc6 deleted) and back 0→1 at 21:08:24 (new pod ...-lkx9d ready 21:08:25); frontend-proxy's error-rate signal was 0 from 21:07:00 to 21:09:00 and non-zero from 21:09:30 onward. Earlier ECONNREFUSED errors at 21:00:58 (product-catalog 10.96.182.202:8080, cart 10.96.88.123:8080) are startup transients of a namespace whose pods were all created at ~21:00:54-21:01:02. All flags in flagd-config are at their off defaults, no pod in otel-demo was ever unready in 21:00-21:13 and no container restart count is above 0, so fault-flag injection, pod eviction/OOM and readiness failures are not supported. The identity of whatever scaled valkey-cart to zero is not known (change history is not integrated), and cart kept logging redis-connection failures at 21:11:19 while the recreated valkey was healthy, so the causal chain from the scale-down to the sustained/error bursts is a strong but unproven hypothesis; conclusion is partial.

claims.text: The firing alert belongs to rule HighRequestErrorRate in rule group opentelemetrydemo.frontend.goldensignal, whose query is sum by (service_name, namespace) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{namespace="otel-demo",service_name=~"frontend|frontend-proxy",status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"}[2m])) > 0 with duration 180; at query time the frontend-proxy alert was in state firing (last evaluation 21:13:12) and a sibling frontend alert was pending, while the annotation template text says "is above 3".

Evaluating the alert expression itself over 21:01:00-21:13:02 gives frontend-proxy error rate 0 at every step from 21:07:00 to 21:09:00 and non-zero values from 21:09:30 onward (1.4357, 2.3605, 1.0556, 2.1556, 1.1, 2.5666666666666664 at 21:12:30, 1.4667 at 21:13:00), while frontend error rate is 0 from 21:07:00 to 21:09:00 and then 2.6354 at 21:09:30 and 9.0667 at 21:12:30; the 2.5666666666666664 reading matches the value in the alert annotation.

frontend-proxy error spans carry status tags error=true with http.status_code 500 on operations GET and POST and http.status_code 504 on a GET that lasted 15000518 us (15s) at 21:12:55, and its client span `router frontend egress` toward the frontend also carries error=true with http.status_code 500 (or http.status_code 0 on the timed-out request), so frontend-proxy's errors are responses/egress calls to the frontend rather than its own downstream dependency.

Frontend spans in the same traces fail with `9 FAILED_PRECONDITION: Can't access cart storage. System.ApplicationException: Wasn't able to connect to redis` (operations executing api route /api/cart and /api/products/[productId]/index, http.status_code 500) and `13 INTERNAL: cart failure: failed to get user cart during checkout`, and frontend client spans `oteldemo.CartService/GetCart` / `oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct` failed with grpc status 14 UNAVAILABLE and `connect ECONNREFUSED 10.96.88.123:8080` / `10.96.182.202:8080` at 21:00:58.

Wasn't able to connect to redis` and `Error status code 'FailedPrecondition' with detail 'Can't access cart storage. System.ApplicationException: Wasn't able to connect to redis'` at 21:08:34-21:08:42 and again at 21:11:19, interleaved with normal GetCartAsync/AddItemAsync lines (e.g. 21:11:20, 21:12:32).

All 24 otel-demo pods report phase Running and ready=true with restartCount 0 (valkey-cart pod created 21:08:24, all other pods created 21:00:54-21:01:02), and no pod in otel-demo had its ready condition false or unknown at any step from 21:02:00 to 21:13:00.

Every flag in ConfigMap flagd-config (data demo.flagd.json) is at its off default: adFailure, adHighCpu, adManualGc, cartFailure, failedReadinessProbe, paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, productCatalogFailure, productCatalogLockContention, recommendationCacheFailure and imageSlowLoad/intlShippingSlowdown/kafkaQueueProblems/loadGeneratorFloodHomepage/aiSlowResponse/aiRunawayAgent/emailMemoryLeak all have defaultVariant "off" (variants off=false or 0).
At 21:09:42 the frontend-proxy span metric shows STATUS_CODE_ERROR rate 0.4889/s against STATUS_CODE_UNSET 21.4704/s, i.e. a small but non-zero error share on the service that owns the alert.

The removal of the valkey-cart pod at 21:08:18 by Deployment valkey-cart's scale-down to 0 is what broke the cart service's redis connection, and the resulting cart FAILED_PRECONDITION storage errors were surfaced by the frontend as HTTP 500/504 responses that frontend-proxy recorded, which is the signal the alert fired on; the timing fits (valkey pod deleted 21:08:18, first redis-connection failure in cart logs 21:08:34-21:08:42, frontend-proxy error rate leaves zero at 21:09:30, alert active from 21:09:42), but cart still logged redis-connection failures at 21:11:19 while the recreated valkey pod was healthy, so the chain is not fully proven.

A second candidate that remains unresolved is a cart-side redis client / connection-state problem independent of the valkey restart, because the same `Wasn't able to connect to redis` errors recur at 21:11:19 while pod valkey-cart-86cdf6f9b9-lkx9d is Running, Ready, restartCount 0 and logged a clean start at 21:08:25; the logs expose only the wrapper message (no inner StackExchange/Redis exception text), so the connection failure mode cannot be determined from this evidence.

Fault-flag injection by flagd is rejected as the cause: every fault-oriented flag (cartFailure, failedReadinessProbe, productCatalogFailure, paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, adFailure, recommendationCacheFailure, kafkaQueueProblems, etc.) has defaultVariant "off" in ConfigMap flagd-config, and the observed cart failure text is a genuine redis connection error rather than a flag-driven fault message.

Pod eviction, OOMKill, crash-loop or readiness failure on the cart path is rejected: the cart pod cart-5bbd5b865c-rvnct is Running and Ready with restartCount 0, no pod in otel-demo was ever not-ready between 21:02:00 and 21:13:00, no otel-demo event other than the valkey-cart scale-down/up and a startup otel-collector probe miss was Warning, and the cart process kept serving successful GetCartAsync/AddItemAsync calls between the error bursts.

product-catalog is not a sustained contributor at the end of the window: at 21:12:00 it had only STATUS_CODE_UNSET spans (12.8519/s) and no STATUS_CODE_ERROR series, its pod product-catalog-658dcdbc87-fvptg is Running/Ready with restartCount 0, and its service has a ready endpoint; its only observed failures are the 21:00:58 ECONNREFUSED spans from the initial startup period.

frontend-proxy itself is not the origin of the failures: its error spans are 500 responses to its callers and failed `router frontend egress` calls to the frontend, i.e. it reports the frontend's failures, while the frontend's error spans and logs carry the cart-storage FAILED_PRECONDITION error text.

Check who scaled Deployment valkey-cart to 0 at 21:08:18 and back to 1 at 21:08:24 (kubectl scale, chaos/test harness or operator) using an audit/change-history source, since the managedFieldsSummary shows no spec write after the helm Apply at 21:00:54 and the change-history integration is not available in this Run.

To confirm the cart-to-valkey link, verify valkey-cart connectivity from the cart pod and look for the inner Redis exception (the container logs only show `Wasn't able to connect to redis` from ValkeyCartStore.EnsureRedisConnected), and consider restarting the cart pod to reset its redis multiplexer if the intermittent FAILED_PRECONDITION errors persist.

The trace view is a biased sample and Jaeger holds only recent traces, so the counts of affected requests and the full call graph behind the frontend 500/504 responses are unknown.
